title: CRISPRi hypomorphs when knockouts are lethal
dek: dCas9 roadblocks make a titratable knockdown — a hypomorph — of genes TnSeq cannot hit. Essential targets (InhA, gyrase, ATP synthase) are studied this way. A knockdown is not a clinical LOF allele.
story: Himar1 cannot knock out a gene that is required for growth: insertions in those TA sites never make the library. CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) uses a catalytically dead Cas9 (dCas9) plus a small guide RNA to block transcription, often at a promoter or the 5′ end of an ORF. The result is a hypomorph: residual expression, not a clean deletion. That is a feature. You can titrate guide strength or inducer and watch fitness fall as a dose–response.

Pooled CRISPRi libraries in Mtb (Rock, Bosch and others in the public literature) turn this into a genome-wide chemical-genetic map: which knockdowns synergise with a drug, which phenocopy a target, which are buffered. This is how you study inhA, gyrA, atpE, and rRNA operon biology without waiting for a viable null.
A clinical frameshift is still not a CRISPRi hypomorph. Knockdown residual protein can keep a complex assembled; a patient LOF may not. Do not equate an sgRNA fitness defect with a WHO catalogue row.
deepTitle: What the method can and cannot claim
deep: Off-target guides and polar operon effects remain. Match phenotypes with a second guide or a rescue plasmid before you name a gene in a paper’s title.
Hypomorph ≠ inhibitor. A drug can inhibit a protein’s activity without lowering its abundance; CRISPRi does the opposite. Agreement is strong evidence; disagreement is not a failed experiment.

atpE is essential; bedaquiline’s clinical resistance is more often Rv0678 efflux than atpE missense. CRISPRi of atpE phenocopies target depletion. It does not predict which allele a cavity will choose.
Essentiality screens and CRISPRi are complementary: TnSeq maps where insertions are allowed; CRISPRi maps how much expression you can remove. Cite both if you argue a target.
Do not put sgRNA IDs on a clinical DST report.

visual.caption: Inducer and sgRNA recruit dCas9 to a promoter or 5′ ORF, lowering transcript and making a hypomorph. Fitness is the readout. A patient LOF allele is a different arrow (DNA change, often zero protein), not a node on this map.

example.title: inhA knockdown is not c-15t
example.setup: A CRISPRi guide against inhA drops growth and raises INH sensitivity in broth. A student concludes that inhA promoter-up (c-15t) should behave as the opposite hypomorph and therefore “proves” low-level INH-R in a patient without a catalogue grade.

steps.title: Opposite directions
steps.body: CRISPRi lowers InhA. c-15t increases inhA transcription. One is a lab hypomorph; the other is a clinical overexpression allele. They are not a paired clinical trial.

steps.title: What still transfers
steps.body: Both argue that InhA level modulates INH phenotypic MIC. Catalogue grading of c-15t still comes from genotype–phenotype datasets, not from an sgRNA.

steps.title: Essentiality link
steps.body: You can CRISPRi inhA because a complete knockout is not viable on plates. That matches the essentiality plate. It still does not belong in the EMB column of a report.

example.takeaway: Hypomorphs titrate essentials. Clinical alleles are a different mutagenesis.

check.prompt: CRISPRi in this teaching sense uses dCas9 to:
choices: Cut both DNA strands and delete the gene
Block transcription, leaving the DNA sequence intact, producing a knockdown (hypomorph)
check.answer: Block transcription, leaving the DNA sequence intact, producing a knockdown (hypomorph)
check.why: Dead Cas9 is a roadblock, not a nuclease in CRISPRi.

whyWrong.Cut both DNA strands and delete the gene: That is CRISPR cutting, not interference.

check.prompt: Two guides reduce a target to 20% and 50% of transcript. Fitness is 0.2 and 0.7 relative to uninduced. This pattern is most consistent with:
choices: A binary essential/non-essential TnSeq call and nothing else
A titratable hypomorph: more knockdown, more fitness cost, without claiming a patient LOF
Proof that the gene is dispensable on plates
check.answer: A titratable hypomorph: more knockdown, more fitness cost, without claiming a patient LOF
check.why: Dose–response is the point of CRISPRi on essentials.

whyWrong.Proof that the gene is dispensable on pl: Fitness 0.2 argues it is important in this condition.

check.prompt: On the mechanism map, why does the promoter node still say “DNA still intact”?
choices: Because CRISPRi is a transcriptional knockdown, not a sequence change like a clinical frameshift
Because dCas9 always mutates the PAM
Because DNA is irrelevant to CFU
Because Himar1 sits on the same node
check.answer: Because CRISPRi is a transcriptional knockdown, not a sequence change like a clinical frameshift
check.why: The contrast with patient LOF is the clinical hygiene of the plate.

whyWrong.Because Himar1 sits on the same node: Himar1 inserts; it does not sit here.
